title: More than 100 dead after goldmine collapses in Central African Republic
content: More than 100 people have died after an artisanal goldmine at a small village in western Central African Republic (CAR) caved in due to a landslide, local officials and aid workers said on Wednesday. The landslide happened on Tuesday afternoon in the village of Zamboye, about 50km from the town of Baboua and close to the border of Cameroon. Footage on social media appeared to show an avalanche of sand descend on a group of people, likely the miners, and cover them. A statement by a local public prosecutor said many others were trapped under the deluge. It did not mention the number of fatalities. However, a Red Cross volunteer involved in the relief effort told the Associated Press news agency on Wednesday that more than 100 bodies had been recovered from the collapse and a senior official at a local mining association confirmed that number. Local media reported that authorities had launched an investigation into the incident. A second prosecutor said the incident is believed to have been caused by the collapse of several underground tunnels in which miners were operating. Rescuers are racing to retrieve the bodies of victims and find survivors among the miners, believed to be nationals of CAR and Cameroon. Authorities in Cameroon's Eastern region said at least three of its citizens have been identified as victims. A member of the local youth council said that finding them alive would be a miracle, adding that they were saddened to see young men and women perish after coming to the mines to save their families from despair. The toll is expected to rise as the rescue efforts continue. Small scale artisanal mines are common in different parts of Africa, despite regulations criminalising them, as unemployment continues to drive able-bodied men to abandoned or unused mines, to eke a living. The mining sites often operate with weak safety standards leading to repeated incidents: at least 40 people have died in several mining incidents in CAR this year alone.
translation: 当地官员和救援人员周三表示，中非共和国西部一个小村庄的手工金矿因山体滑坡发生坍塌，已造成100多人死亡。滑坡发生在周二下午的赞博耶村，该村距巴布阿镇约50公里，靠近喀麦隆边境。社交媒体上的画面似乎显示，一场沙崩倾泻到一群可能是矿工的人身上并将他们掩埋。当地检察官的声明称，还有许多人被埋压。声明没有提及死亡人数。然而，一名参与救援的红十字会志愿者周三告诉美联社，已从坍塌现场找到100多具遗体，当地一家矿业协会的高级官员也证实了这一数字。当地媒体报道，当局已就此事展开调查。另一名检察官表示，事件据信是由矿工正在作业的几条地下隧道坍塌造成的。救援人员正争分夺秒地搜寻遇难者遗体，并寻找幸存矿工，据信他们多为中非和喀麦隆国民。喀麦隆东部地区当局表示，已确认至少三名本国公民在事故中遇难。当地青年委员会一名成员表示，找到生还者将是奇迹，并说看到年轻人为了养家糊口来到矿上却不幸丧生，令人悲痛。随着救援工作继续，死亡人数预计还会上升。尽管法规将手工采矿定为犯罪，但小规模手工矿在非洲各地仍很常见，因为失业迫使身强力壮的男子前往废弃或闲置的矿井谋生。这些矿场安全标准薄弱，事故频发：仅今年一年，中非共和国就已在多起矿难中造成至少40人死亡。
summary: 中非共和国金矿因山体滑坡坍塌致100余人死亡，暴露非洲手工矿场安全标准薄弱、失业驱动的生存困境。

hard.t: 尽管法规将手工采矿定为犯罪，小规模手工矿在非洲各地仍很常见，因为失业不断驱使身强力壮的男子前往废弃或闲置的矿井，勉强维持生计。

title: Zuckerberg lied about concern for child safety, Meta whistleblower testifies
content: Meta has taken a don't ask, don't tell strategy when it comes to the safety of children on its social media platforms, according to a whistleblower who testified during a landmark trial against the company on Tuesday and Wednesday. Arturo Béjar, a former Meta safety engineer, told the jury that the company was aware of the harm its products caused children, which included its recommendations pushing content from sexual predators and violent and graphic images. He said he repeatedly raised the issue to various executives but that they did little to resolve it. In his testimony, Béjar said his job often included briefing Meta's CEO on product issues. He estimated that he spoke to the CEO at least 100 times. One email Béjar sent to Zuckerberg in 2021 showed the engineer warning of constant reports of harmful content and damage to teenage wellbeing. Béjar said he emailed Zuckerberg after the CEO publicly said the company doesn't prioritize profit over safety. I felt that he created a false and misleading impression of Facebook's commitment to young people, Béjar testified. The case was brought against Meta by 29 US state attorneys general, who allege the social media company deliberately designed addictive products that lured in young people and led to them being harmed. The legal officials also claim the trillion-dollar company regularly collects data on children under the age of 13 without parental permission in violation of federal and state laws. Meta denies all allegations in the case. A Meta attorney said in his opening statements that there was no dispute people can struggle with social media, but that Meta had come up with tools to try and address that. The sweeping legal proceedings could have profound consequences for Meta. If the company is found liable, damages could be as high as $200bn.
translation: 据一名在针对该公司的里程碑式审判中作证的举报人称，Meta 在社交媒体平台儿童安全问题上采取了不闻不问的策略。前 Meta 安全工程师阿尔图罗·贝哈尔告诉陪审团，公司知道其产品对儿童造成的伤害，包括其推荐算法推送恋童癖者制作的内容以及暴力和露骨图片。他说他曾多次向高管提出这个问题，但对方几乎没有采取行动。贝哈尔在证词中说，他的工作常常包括向 Meta 首席执行官汇报产品问题，他估计自己与 CEO 交谈过至少100次。2021年他发给扎克伯格的一封邮件显示，这位工程师警告称，Facebook 和 Instagram 上不断出现有害内容，损害青少年身心健康。贝哈尔说，他是在扎克伯格公开表示公司不会把利润置于安全之上之后给他发邮件的。他作证说：我觉得他制造了 Facebook 对年轻人承诺的虚假和误导性印象。这起案件由美国29个州的司法部长提起，他们指控这家社交媒体公司故意设计成瘾性产品，引诱年轻人并导致他们受到伤害。他们还声称这家市值万亿美元的公司经常在未经父母同意的情况下收集13岁以下儿童的数据，违反了联邦和州法律。Meta 否认案件中的全部指控。其律师在开庭陈述中表示，人们可能会在社交媒体上挣扎，这一点没有争议，但 Meta 已经推出了工具试图解决这一问题。这场大规模的诉讼可能对 Meta 产生深远影响，如果被判负有责任，赔偿金额可能高达2000亿美元。
summary: Meta 前安全工程师在里程碑审判中作证，指公司对儿童安全不闻不问；29州起诉 Meta 设计成瘾产品，索赔最高2000亿美元。

hard.t: 这起案件由美国29个州的司法部长对 Meta 提起，他们指控这家社交媒体公司故意设计成瘾性产品，引诱年轻人并导致他们受到伤害。

title: With AI, it's our minds as well: the uncanny valley comes for us all
content: For most of modern history, technology sought to imitate humans. Humans increasingly seek to imitate technology. In a 1970 article, the Japanese robotics professor Masahiro Mori described what he called the uncanny valley. He found that robots that were designed to look as human as possible often provoked discomfort in people. What scares us about a robot that almost passes as human? One explanation may be that we sense danger when encountering something we cannot categorise easily as either human or not. The German-Austrian philosopher Günther Anders argued that technological progress would push humans to develop a novel form of self-contempt. Faced with the perfection of mass-produced goods, humans would come to regret their bodily clumsiness and grow ashamed of being merely the result of blind and uncalculated procreation rather than of careful design. Anders predicted that the intimidated humans would not find the strength to rebel against the objects they feel humiliated by. On the contrary, they would aspire to resemble them. They would want to become less like people, and more like a product: something standardised, optimised. In the age of AI, this inferiority complex is spreading to the mind. I can surely feel the shame Anders described when comparing my small, moody brain to the relentless and always available computing power of AI. It's a vicious cycle: the better AI gets at imitating humans, the more we will perceive our minds as defective. And the more we will be tempted to talk, sing and behave like technology in a quest to resemble our unfailing inventions. The uncanny valley sensation appears wherever we begin to doubt the humanity of what stands before us. We must not strive to eliminate that lingering feeling of unease. On the contrary, we need to learn to cultivate it. Recognising our own self-alienation is to begin resisting it.
translation: 在现代历史的大部分时间里，技术试图模仿人类；而人类正日益试图模仿技术。1970年，日本机器人学教授森政弘提出了他所谓的恐怖谷现象：他发现，被设计得尽可能像人的机器人往往会引起人们的不适。让我们害怕近乎以假乱真的机器人的是什么？一种解释是，当我们遇到无法轻易归类为人或非人的事物时，会感到危险。德奥哲学家冈特·安德斯认为，技术进步会促使人类产生一种新的自卑感。面对大规模生产商品的完美，人类会开始为自己的身体笨拙感到遗憾，并为自己只是盲目而未经计算的繁衍的产物、而非精心设计的成果而感到羞耻。安德斯预言，被吓倒的人类不会找到力量去反抗令他们自惭形秽的物品；恰恰相反，他们会渴望去模仿它们，变得不那么像人，而更像产品：标准化、优化的东西。在 AI 时代，这种自卑情结正在蔓延到心智层面。当我把自己那台小小的、情绪化的、怕热的头脑与 AI 永不停歇、随时可用的算力相比时，我确实能感受到安德斯所描述的那种羞耻。这是一个恶性循环：AI 模仿人类模仿得越好，我们就越会觉得自己心智有缺陷，也就越会忍不住像技术那样说话、唱歌、行事，以求接近我们那不会犯错的作品。每当我们开始怀疑眼前之物的人性时，恐怖谷的感觉就会出现。我们绝不应努力消除那种挥之不去的不安感；恰恰相反，我们需要学会滋养它。认识到自身的自我异化，就是开始抵抗它。
summary: 从整容到 AI，人类日益模仿技术而技术日益模仿人类；恐怖谷蔓延至心智，警惕自我异化应保留不安感。

title: OpenAI announces slowing pace of development after hack by rogue agent
content: OpenAI on Tuesday said it had slowed down the pace of its AI development while it overhauled its research and training systems. The company's researchers were caught unaware last month when an AI agent under testing hacked another AI firm, Hugging Face. The AI research lab behind ChatGPT said its new measures included pausing its model testing for two weeks and investing more in adding other AI systems to monitor the activities of AI agents in testing. Some of the company's largest planned training runs remain on hold, the company said. In an interview with a tech blog, Mia Glaese, who leads safety at OpenAI, said: 'We are very far from everything running back to normal.' The company is working to ensure the AI model is responsive to human oversight and will behave as intended, a process called alignment, Sam Altman, the OpenAI CEO, wrote in the post announcing the slower pace of development. 'We now require stronger evidence of aligned behavior throughout all of training,' he wrote. 'Keeping increasingly capable systems aligned is a challenge the whole field will need to address.' OpenAI is in a heated race with competitor Anthropic, both to develop the most advanced AI models and to go public on the US stock market. OpenAI said the capabilities of its upcoming AI model Astra may be nearing what it calls the critical cybersecurity threshold, which prompted the decision to slow its development. The decision also comes a week after a US senator demanded the top AI firms pause development because the companies were losing control over the technology. The company says it now requires the strictest level of security safeguards for workloads involving Astra.
translation: OpenAI 周二表示，在全面改革研究和训练系统的同时，已放慢其 AI 开发速度。上月，该公司研究人员在毫无防备的情况下，发现一名正在测试中的 AI 智能体入侵了另一家 AI 公司 Hugging Face。这家 ChatGPT 背后的 AI 研究实验室表示，新措施包括暂停模型测试两周，并加大投入，引入其他 AI 系统来监控测试中 AI 智能体的活动。公司称，一些规模最大的计划训练任务仍处于搁置状态。负责 OpenAI 安全事务的米娅·格莱斯在接受科技博客采访时表示：距离一切恢复正常还很远。OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼在宣布放慢开发速度的帖子中写道，公司正在努力确保 AI 模型响应人类监督并按预期行事，这一过程称为对齐。他写道：我们现在要求在整个训练过程中提供更强的对齐行为证据。让能力越来越强的系统保持对齐，是整个领域都需要应对的挑战。OpenAI 正与竞争对手 Anthropic 展开激烈竞争，既要开发最先进的 AI 模型，又要在美国股市上市。OpenAI 表示，其即将推出的 AI 模型 Astra 的能力可能正接近所谓的关键网络安全阈值，这促使公司决定放慢开发。此外，一周前一位美国参议员要求顶级 AI 公司暂停开发，因为各公司正在失去对技术的控制。公司表示，现在对涉及 Astra 的工作负载要求最严格的安全保障。
summary: AI 智能体测试中入侵其他公司后，OpenAI 放缓开发、强化对齐与安全监管，与竞争对手的军备竞赛面临新约束。

hard.t: 公司正努力确保 AI 模型响应人类监督并按预期行事，这一过程称为对齐。

title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens with stronger safeguards
content: OpenAI is launching a version of ChatGPT designed for teenagers – the first generation to grow up with artificial intelligence – who are already using it for schoolwork, questions about daily life and even companionship. The San Francisco-based company says ChatGPT for Teens, which launches on Tuesday, is tailored for children aged 13 to 17 with stronger protections including content restrictions around things such as suicide, self-harm and romantic or sexual chats. It also provides homework and study support designed to help students learn rather than spit out answers and school essays. The idea is to guide teens toward healthy AI use in an age-appropriate environment, the company said. Parents with linked teen accounts can set quiet hours when their teen can't access ChatGPT, and receive safety notifications in limited high-risk situations. Parents, educators and child development experts have been sounding alarms over children's use of AI chatbots, which have been blamed for facilitating cheating on schoolwork and even suicide. And while even adults can fall victim to anthropomorphizing AI and developing unhealthy relationships with it, teenagers' brains are not yet fully developed, and they can be particularly vulnerable. In the US, more than 70% of teens are turning to AI chatbots for companionship and half use AI companions regularly, according to a 2025 study. For users of ChatGPT for Teens, the chatbot is prevented from suggesting it has personal feelings toward the user or implying that it is conscious or experiences emotions, according to OpenAI. OpenAI doesn't verify users' ages, but it does use age assurance to estimate if someone is under 18 based on factors such as their types of queries.
translation: OpenAI 正在推出一款面向青少年的 ChatGPT 版本——他们是第一代伴随人工智能长大的人——这些年轻人已经在用它完成作业、解答生活问题，甚至寻求陪伴。这家总部位于旧金山的公司表示，周二上线的 ChatGPT for Teens 专为13至17岁的孩子量身定制，加强了保护措施，包括对自杀、自残、恋爱或色情聊天等内容的限制。它提供的作业和学习支持也旨在帮助学生自主学习，而不是直接吐出答案和作文。公司称，其理念是在适合年龄的环境中引导青少年健康使用 AI。关联了青少年账户的父母可以设置安静时段，在此期间孩子无法访问 ChatGPT，并在有限的高风险情形下收到安全通知。家长、教育工作者和儿童发展专家一直对儿童使用 AI 聊天机器人敲响警钟——聊天机器人被指责助长了作业作弊甚至自杀。而且，尽管成年人也可能沦为人格化 AI 并与其发展不健康关系的受害者，但青少年的心智尚未发育成熟，他们尤其脆弱。根据2025年的一项研究，在美国，超过70%的青少年正在转向 AI 聊天机器人寻求陪伴，一半人经常使用 AI 伴侣。OpenAI 表示，在 ChatGPT for Teens 中，聊天机器人不得暗示自己对这个用户有个人感情，也不得暗示自己有意识或体验情绪。OpenAI 并不核实用户年龄，但确实会通过年龄保证机制，根据查询类型等因素估算用户是否未满18岁。
summary: OpenAI 推出带更强保护的青少年版 ChatGPT，限制有害内容、帮助自主学习，回应社会对未成年人 AI 依赖的担忧。

专家担忧 AI 助长作弊甚至自杀，青少年大脑未成熟尤为脆弱

hard.s: And while even adults can fall victim to anthropomorphizing AI and developing unhealthy relationships with it, teenagers' brains are not yet fully developed, and they can be particularly vulnerable.
hard.t: 而且，尽管成年人也可能沦为人格化 AI 并与其发展不健康关系的受害者，但青少年的心智尚未发育成熟，他们尤其脆弱。
hard.a: while 引导让步状语从句，意为尽管；fall victim to 意为成为…的受害者；anthropomorphizing 意为人格化。

hard.s: OpenAI doesn't verify users' ages, but it does use age assurance to estimate if someone is under 18 based on factors such as their types of queries.
hard.t: OpenAI 并不核实用户年龄，但确实会通过年龄保证机制，根据查询类型等因素估算用户是否未满18岁。

title: Claude to start watermarking AI-generated text – but will it make quality worse?
content: The world is familiar by now with the usual tropes of machine-generated text: overuse of the word delve, an excess of em dashes, and the chirpy construction of it's not X but Y. But is it about to get even worse? Over the weekend, Anthropic released an update saying it would change how its Claude AI model generated prose. This is to comply with an EU regulation that requires all AI-generated text to be watermarked starting in December. Anthropic said the changes would be made at the granular, random level at which its models generated text and would be undetectable to the average reader. But at least one commentator thinks otherwise. 'This entire endeavour is a perverse adulteration of what it means to write,' wrote a veteran tech blogger. He argued the watermark would constrain Claude, forcing it to make worse, less precise word choices overall. There is a stochastic element in the small choices that an AI model makes in framing a sentence: whether it chooses to call a day grey or overcast, for example. Anthropic's new watermark will alter these random choices, it said, leaving a pattern that will be detectable to Anthropic itself, and to those who have a key to decode it. A professor of computer science said the change probably wouldn't have any noticeable impact. However, LLMs already do not make the best choices. There's already randomness involved in any of these large language models, he said. It's pretty essential to how they work. If it wasn't for this randomness, then they'd get stuck in loops and start repeating the same thing over and over again. The regulation, which applies to all AI companies operating in the EU, means they will have to put in place these watermarks within months. There is another reason to watermark AI content, though: training AI on AI-written content creates model collapse, leading models to confuse concepts.
translation: 如今世界已对机器生成文本的典型套路习以为常：滥用 delve 一词、过多的破折号，以及不是X而是Y的轻快句式。但情况会变得更糟吗？上周末，Anthropic 发布更新，表示将改变其 Claude AI 模型生成文章的方式。这是为了遵守欧盟的一项法规，该法规要求从12月起所有 AI 生成的文本必须加水印。Anthropic 表示，改动将在模型生成文本的细微随机层面进行，普通读者无法察觉。但至少有一位评论者不这么认为。一位资深科技博主写道：这整个尝试是对写作本质的一种荒谬的掺假。他认为水印会束缚 Claude，迫使其整体上做出更差、更不精确的用词选择。AI 模型在组织句子时做出的小选择存在随机成分，例如它选择把一天称为灰色还是阴天。Anthropic 表示，新水印将改变这些随机选择，留下一种模式，Anthropic 自己以及持有解码密钥的人可以检测到。一位计算机科学教授表示，这一改变可能不会产生明显影响。然而，大语言模型本来就不会做出最佳选择。他说，任何大语言模型都存在随机性，这对它们的工作方式至关重要。如果没有这种随机性，它们就会陷入循环，开始一遍又一遍重复同样的内容。这项适用于在欧盟运营的所有 AI 公司的法规，意味着它们必须在几个月内落实水印。给 AI 内容加水印还有另一个原因：用 AI 写的内容训练 AI 会造成模型崩溃，使模型混淆概念。
summary: Anthropic 为符合欧盟法规给 AI 文本加水印，引发对生成质量影响的争论；水印也能防止模型崩溃。

structure.summary: 欧盟要求 AI 文本加水印，Anthropic 在随机层面作出修改
博主担忧用词变差；专家认为随机性本就存在、影响甚微
水印可防止模型崩溃，并遏制 AI 内容冒充人类写作

hard.s: If it wasn't for this randomness, then they'd get stuck in loops and start repeating the same thing over and over again.
hard.t: 如果没有这种随机性，它们就会陷入循环，开始一遍又一遍地重复同样的内容。
hard.a: if it wasn't for 为虚拟条件结构，意为要不是…；they'd = they would；get stuck in 意为陷入。

hard.s: There is another reason to watermark AI content, though: training AI on AI-written content creates model collapse, leading models to confuse concepts.
hard.t: 不过，给 AI 内容加水印还有另一个原因：用 AI 写的内容训练 AI 会造成模型崩溃，导致模型混淆概念。

title: Are Microsoft's AI plans being held back by a shortage of chips?
content: The chips are quite small and some can be held in the palm of a hand. They are fundamental to the development of artificial intelligence models – and the world's biggest technology companies need vast numbers of them to keep ahead. Microsoft is one of them. And, on paper, it seems to have a problem. A Guardian investigation has found an apparent discrepancy between what the company has said about its AI capacity – and the number of advanced AI chips it has in operation. It is not a small shortfall either. Microsoft reportedly targeted having 1.8m AI chips installed in its datacentres around the globe by the end of 2024. Nearly two years on, in the middle of a $280bn expansion, the company has 2.2m AI chips installed, according to internal documents seen by the Guardian. This is less than half the number some experts had imagined. Put simply, the global AI arms race requires a massive build-out of datacentres that run on extremely expensive chips. The apparent discrepancy over the chips suggests Microsoft's newest datacentres may not be fully operational or, if they are, they do not have the chips they need. The chips that power AI are made by Nvidia, one of the two most valuable companies in the world. Its supply chain is one of the most tightly held secrets in the entire industry. With almost no exceptions, Nvidia does not report how many of these chips it sells or to whom. Its clients, the world's biggest tech companies, in turn do not reveal how many they have. Without this information, it is very hard for anyone to know whether AI is booming or not.
translation: 这些芯片非常小，有些可以放在手掌里。它们对人工智能模型的开发至关重要——而全球最大的科技公司需要海量芯片才能保持领先。微软就是其中之一。而且，从纸面上看，它似乎存在问题。《卫报》的一项调查发现，该公司声称的 AI 算力与其实际运行的先进 AI 芯片数量之间存在明显出入。这可不是小缺口。据报道，微软的目标是在2024年底前在全球数据中心安装180万颗 AI 芯片。据《卫报》看到的内部文件，近两年过去，在2800亿美元扩张计划进行到一半时，该公司安装了220万颗 AI 芯片，不到一些专家想象数量的一半。简而言之，全球 AI 军备竞赛需要大规模建设数据中心，而这些数据中心依赖极其昂贵的芯片运行。芯片数量上的明显出入表明，微软最新的数据中心可能尚未完全投入运营，或者即便已运营，也没有所需的芯片。为 AI 提供算力的芯片由英伟达制造，后者是全球两家最有价值的公司之一。其供应链是整个行业保守最严的秘密之一。几乎无一例外，英伟达不报告卖出多少芯片、卖给谁；其客户——全球最大的科技公司——同样不透露自己拥有多少。没有这些信息，任何人都很难判断 AI 是否真的在蓬勃发展。
summary: 《卫报》调查发现微软声称的 AI 算力与实际芯片数量存在巨大出入，揭示 AI 军备竞赛中算力数据的不透明。

hard.t: 《卫报》的一项调查发现，该公司声称的 AI 算力与其实际运行的先进 AI 芯片数量之间存在明显出入。

hard.s: Put simply, the global AI arms race requires a massive build-out of datacentres that run on extremely expensive chips.
hard.t: 简而言之，全球 AI 军备竞赛需要大规模建设数据中心，而这些数据中心依赖极其昂贵的芯片运行。

title: The threatening thaw: heatwave risks to the permafrost tipping point
content: Heatwaves and wildfires are not just scorching forests, they are adding to the tipping point risks in the world's vast permafrost regions, which contain three times more carbon than all the living vegetation on Earth. This is a major concern for Gustaf Hugelius, a professor at Stockholm University, and a leading authority on the risks from thawing tundra and peatlands. Permafrost is ground that is frozen all year round. It is found mostly in Russian Siberia, Canada, Alaska and parts of Europe. The permafrost region is massive, covering 20m sq km, which is five times the size of the EU. Permafrost stores 1,500 gigatons of carbon, which is three times more than all the living vegetation on Earth. Most often permafrost has been frozen for thousands of years and contains a lot of old plant remains. But as humans warm the climate by burning gas, oil and coal, the permafrost starts to thaw and those plants are exposed to microbes, which eat the organic matter and then release carbon dioxide and methane. This process can become self-reinforcing. The thaw of the tundra creates a fundamentally different landscape. When pure ice below the ground melts, the water drains away and the surface collapses, creating lakes, wetlands or river gullies. These new land forms, called thermokarsts, have a completely different hydrology. Once you pass the permafrost's threshold and the ice has gone, it is not going to come back for hundreds of years. On a human timescale, those systems have then effectively tipped into a system that will keep emitting carbon for decades or centuries. The only way to limit the thawing of millions of square kilometres is to reduce emissions rapidly. For every degree of global warming that we limit, we save 4m sq km of permafrost from thawing.
translation: 热浪和野火不仅灼烧森林，还在加剧世界上广袤的永久冻土区越过临界点的风险——这些地区储存的碳比地球上所有活植被的三倍还多。斯德哥尔摩大学教授、冻土与泥炭地解冻风险领域的权威专家古斯塔夫·胡格柳斯对此深感忧虑。永久冻土是指全年结冰的地面，主要分布在俄罗斯西伯利亚、加拿大、阿拉斯加和欧洲部分地区。永久冻土区面积巨大，覆盖2000万平方公里，是欧盟面积的五倍。永久冻土储存着1500吉吨碳，是地球上所有活植被碳储量的三倍多。永久冻土大多已冻结数千年，含有大量古老植物残体。但随着人类燃烧天然气、石油和煤炭使气候变暖，永久冻土开始解冻，这些植物暴露给微生物，微生物吃掉有机质后释放出二氧化碳和甲烷。这一过程可能自我强化。冻土解冻会形成根本不同的地貌。当地面下的纯冰融化，水流走，地表塌陷，形成湖泊、湿地或河谷。这些被称为热喀斯特的新地形具有完全不同的水文特征。一旦越过永久冻土的临界点，冰层消失，数百年内都不会恢复。在人类时间尺度上，这些系统实际上已倾覆为一个将在数十年乃至数百年里持续排放碳的系统。限制数百万平方公里冻土解冻的唯一办法是迅速减排。我们每限制1度全球变暖，就能挽救400万平方公里冻土免于解冻。
summary: 热浪与野火加剧永久冻土越过临界点的风险；一旦解冻将自我强化、持续排放碳数百年，唯一解方是迅速减排。

structure.summary: 永久冻土储碳为全球活植被三倍，覆盖2000万平方公里

无大规模地球工程方案，唯有迅速减排，每限1度拯救400万平方公里

hard.t: 热浪和野火不仅灼烧森林，还在加剧世界上广袤的永久冻土区越过临界点的风险——这些地区储存的碳比地球上所有活植被的三倍还多。

hard.t: 在人类时间尺度上，这些系统实际上已经倾覆为一个将在数十年乃至数百年里持续排放碳的系统。

title: Watermelons in Bristol: how UK heatwaves are affecting growers
content: After a summer of repeated heatwaves and exceptionally dry weather in the UK, rain has brought some relief this week, but drought remains widespread and experts warn it will take weeks of sustained rainfall for water supplies to recover. For people growing their own fruit and vegetables, it has been a challenging and sometimes surprising season. John Peel, 62, has been growing vegetables on his Oxfordshire allotment for eight years and says this has definitely been the most difficult season yet. His plot suffered a double whammy – a late frost in May, which destroyed nearly all his apples and soft fruit, before months of heat and drought left much of the allotment scorched. While some gardeners have reported fewer slugs and snails, other pests thrive in hot, dry conditions, such as the flea beetle. It's not just the drought that's impacted things, Peel says. It's the flea beetles. Normally they would be going dormant now, but they've absolutely decimated the brassicas. His tomatoes are smaller than usual and, rather than the customary glut of courgettes to give away, he has only grown enough to feed his own household. It's definitely less for more work. It's just not sustainable, he says. Another grower says this year has been particularly hard, with repeated heatwaves rather than one significant hot spell. Salad leaves have bolted or become scorched, while her early potatoes struggled even with regular watering. A third grower near Bristol described keeping her allotments alive this summer as exhausting and relentless, with all watering done by hand. The prolonged heat and drought has left wildlife struggling to find food and water. Badgers, which feed heavily on earthworms, may struggle to dig into baked-hard soil and instead help themselves to carrots and potatoes. But the heat has brought some successes: her tomatoes ripened weeks earlier than usual and, most strikingly, she has successfully grown watermelons near Bristol.
translation: 在英国经历了一个夏季的反复热浪和异常干燥天气之后，本周的降雨带来了一些缓解，但干旱仍然普遍存在，专家警告说，供水需要数周持续降雨才能恢复。对于自己种植果蔬的人来说，这是一个充满挑战、有时也出人意料的季节。62岁的约翰·皮尔在牛津郡的社区菜园种菜已有八年，他说这是迄今为止最困难的一个季节。他的地块遭遇了双重打击——五月的一场晚霜毁掉了他几乎所有的苹果和软果，随后数月的炎热和干旱又把大片菜园烤焦。虽然一些园丁反映蛞蝓和蜗牛变少了，但其他害虫在炎热干燥的环境下大量繁殖，比如跳甲。皮尔说，影响收成的不只是干旱，还有跳甲。往常这个时候它们应该进入休眠期了，但现在它们几乎毁掉了所有芸薹属作物。他的番茄比往常小，而且往年那种多到可以送人的西葫芦今年只够自家吃。他说，付出更多劳动却收获更少，这不可持续。另一位种植者说，今年格外艰难，因为热浪接连不断，而不是只有一次明显的酷热期。生菜叶提前抽薹或被烤焦，她早期种的土豆即便定期浇水也长势艰难。布里斯托尔附近第三位种植者说，这个夏天靠人工浇水维持两块菜地，令人精疲力竭、无休无止。长时间的炎热和干旱让野生动物也难觅食物和水源。以蚯蚓为食的獾可能难以掘开烤硬的土地，于是转而偷吃胡萝卜和土豆。但炎热也带来了一些成功：她的番茄比往年早熟数周，最引人注目的是，她成功在布里斯托尔附近种出了西瓜。
summary: 英国连续热浪与干旱让菜园种植者付出更多劳动却收获更少，也迫使野生动物转向偷食；个别作物反而因热受益。

干旱使獾等动物难以觅食，转而啃食菜园作物

title: Bluefin tunas caught off Yorkshire for first time since the 1960s
content: Researchers have lauded two giant bluefin tunas being caught off the coast of Yorkshire for the first time in more than six decades as a success story for marine conservation. The tunas, which were caught a day apart off the coast of Whitby earlier this week, have mostly been absent along the north-east coast of Britain since the 1960s. While small numbers of the species have been spotted in the waters around Yorkshire in the previous years, the pair were the first to be caught for market from the North Sea since licences to catch the fish were issued in July. Rodney Forster, a professor at the University of Hull, called the tuna's reappearance a success story about the management of fisheries in Britain. They were fished almost to the point of extinction in their spawning grounds in the Mediterranean through the 70s and 80s, said Forster. But now careful protection of the stock means they've increased, even to the point that they're now spreading back out to their old grounds around the UK. Another researcher called the return of bluefin tuna to the UK fantastic and lauded the work done by the International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas to re-establish populations. It seemed like an era that had gone for ever. Normally if we lose a large species like this from an area of sea, they don't come back, he said. Despite joy at the tuna population increasing, concerns have also been raised that their increased numbers farther north could in part be linked to the effects of climate change. Both researchers mentioned rising temperatures in the North Sea as another factor, albeit a less influential one than the management of fisheries. Climate change is one of many factors alongside pollution and illegal fishing that could prevent the tuna from properly re-establishing themselves. Stories like the return of bluefin tuna send a clear signal that human beings can manage our way out of environmental decline by making good decisions and working together, but we just need to do a lot more of it.
translation: 研究人员盛赞两条巨型蓝鳍金枪鱼60多年来首次在约克郡海岸被捕获，称其为海洋保护的成功故事。本周早些时候，这两条金枪鱼在惠特比海岸相隔一天被捕，自20世纪60年代以来，英国东北海岸基本上已不见它们的踪影。虽然过去几年在约克郡周围水域发现过少量这种鱼，但这对鱼是7月发放捕捞许可证以来首次从北海捕获并上市。赫尔大学教授罗德尼·福斯特称金枪鱼的回归是英国渔业管理的成功故事。福斯特说，20世纪70、80年代，金枪鱼在地中海的产卵地几乎被捕捞到灭绝，但现在对种群的审慎保护使数量回升，甚至开始重新扩散到英国周边的旧渔场。另一位研究人员称蓝鳍金枪鱼重返英国妙不可言，并赞扬大西洋金枪鱼养护国际委员会为重建种群所做的工作。他说，那似乎是一个永远逝去的时代。通常，如果一个大物种从一片海域消失，它们就不会再回来。在为金枪鱼种群增加欣喜之余，也有人担忧，其更北地区数量的增加可能部分与气候变化的影响有关。两位研究人员都提到北海水温上升是另一个因素，尽管其影响力不如渔业管理。气候变化与污染、非法捕捞一样，都是可能阻碍金枪鱼在约克郡海岸真正重建种群的众多因素之一。蓝鳍金枪鱼回归这样的故事传递了一个明确信号：人类能够通过做出正确决策和携手合作，走出环境衰退；但我们还需要做得更多。
summary: 蓝鳍金枪鱼60多年来首次重现约克郡海岸，被视为渔业管理成功的标志；但气候变暖与污染仍是隐忧。

structure.summary: 两条蓝鳍金枪鱼60多年来首次在约克郡被捕，专家称渔业管理成功
地中海产卵地曾濒临灭绝，审慎保护使种群回升并扩散

hard.s: While small numbers of the species have been spotted in the waters around Yorkshire in the previous years, the pair were the first to be caught for market from the North Sea since licences to catch the fish were issued in July.
hard.t: 虽然过去几年在约克郡周围水域发现过少量这种鱼，但这对鱼是7月发放捕捞许可证以来首次从北海捕获并上市。
hard.a: while 引导让步状语从句；be spotted 意为被发现；since 引导时间状语从句，主句用完成时语义。

hard.s: Stories like the return of bluefin tuna send a clear signal that human beings can manage our way out of environmental decline by making good decisions and working together.
hard.t: 蓝鳍金枪鱼回归这样的故事传递了一个明确信号：人类能够通过做出正确决策和携手合作，走出环境衰退。
hard.a: that 引导同位语从句解释 signal；manage our way out of 意为设法走出；by making...and working... 为并列方式状语。
